title: telemetry-bridge-design-and-tf-modules-draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick-draft playbook for shipping telemetry from VPC/on-prem private deployments into a resilient, low-cost observability stack. Focus: Prometheus metrics (remote-write), Grafana provisioning, OTEL collector topology, log shipper options, and Terraform module layout. This is intentionally rough — want feedback on tradeoffs (Thanos vs Cortex, Vector vs Fluent Bit, sidecar vs relay), and clear upgrade/rollback paths.

Goals / constraints:
- Keep customer data inside VPC unless they opt-in for object storage export (MINIO/S3-compatible).
- Allow multi-tenant on-prem clusters (namespaces) but strict per-customer isolation by routing and auth.
- Support both k8s and bare-metal agent topologies.
- Minimize cardinality and cost; prefer relabeling at the source.
- Terraform-first: infra modules that are reusable across accounts/regions.

High-level design summary:
- Metrics: Local Prometheus (either Node exporter + kube-state) scraping pod/service metrics -> remote_write -> Prometheus remote-write gateway (metrics-relay) -> long-term store (Thanos sidecar + object storage or hosted remote-write endpoint). For small on-prem customers we keep short-term retention only (14d) and enable optional remote archive.
- Logs: Vector as the recommended shipper (lower memory, single binary, built-in transforms). Run as DaemonSet on k8s or systemd-managed agent on VMs. Ship to local ELK stack, MinIO, or central Kafka depending on customer preference.
- Traces: OTEL Collector in two tiers: agent (DaemonSet) + collector relay (Deployment with autoscale). Agent performs batching/compression and basic filtering, relay performs routing, export, and enrichment.
- Dashboards: Grafana deployed either in-cluster (single-tenant) or multi-tenant Grafana Enterprise behind internal LB. Dashboards are provisioned via Grafana provisioning files managed by Terraform + config repo.

Terraform modules (proposal):
- tf-module-telemetry-networking: VPC/subnet routes, security groups for metrics ports (9090, 4317, 4318), LB for relay endpoints, optional VPC peering. Inputs: vpc_id, allowed_cidrs, enable_peering. Outputs: relay_lb_dns, collector_sg_id.
- tf-module-prometheus-cluster: K8s deployment/Helm release wrapper for Prometheus Operator, scrape configs templated, PVC sizing input. Inputs: retention_days, replica_count, pvc_size_gb. Outputs: prometheus_endpoint, rules_configmap_id.
- tf-module-telemetry-store: object storage (MinIO backend) or S3 stub + lifecycle rules. Inputs: storage_class, replication_policy, kms_key. Outputs: bucket_name, endpoint_url.
- tf-module-otel-collector: DaemonSet and relay Deployment manifests (templated), cert manager integration. Inputs: collector_image, relay_replicas, otlp_tls: true/false. Outputs: agent_daemonset_name, relay_service_name.
- tf-module-grafana-provision: provision datasource + dashboard jsons and service account + admin credential rotation. Inputs: datasource_type, dashboards_repo, admin_user. Outputs: grafana_url, datasource_ids.

Key implementation notes / opinionated defaults:
- Default to Thanos for long-term metrics for on-prem because sidecar + object-storage gives predictable egress and cheaper storage profiles; Cortex/Tigris option remains for very high ingestion customers.
- Remote-write gateway (metrics-relay) uses 3 replicas behind LB, accepts Prometheus remote_write with JWT-based client certs for auth. Relay performs relabeling and fan-out to long-term store + short-term Prometheus.
- Cardinality control: ship relabeling at scrape config level and agent-level drops. Provide recommended relabel rules in the module: drop label patterns for pod_template_hash, node affinity labels, and telemetry debug tags.
- Storage sizing heuristic: metrics QPS * avg_series_per_query * retention_days * bytes_per_sample. Example: 2000 samples/s * 1500 series * 14d * 0.025 KB/sample -> ~1.26 TB. (This is a place-holder calc — will refine with real workloads).

OTEL collector topology (example):
- Agent (DaemonSet): scrapes metrics via otlp http/grpc for instrumented apps, collects traces, performs resource attribution, and applies 'drop' processors for noisy spans. For logs, agent applies remap transforms to remove PII fields.
- Relay: 3-5 replicas, accepts compressed batched traffic from agents, implements routing rules by tenant, exports to backends (Jaeger/OTLP exporter to central tracing). Uses mTLS between agent->relay.

Grafana provisioning notes:
- Manage datasources via file provisioning in git repo and have tf-module mount it as a configmap. Use admin password rotation with Vault integration.
- Dashboards: keep canonical dashboards in a dashboards/ repo and import via provisioning. Don't store secrets or API keys in dashboard JSONs.

Logs pipeline options (tradeoffs):
- Vector: recommended. Pros: single binary, memory efficient, rich transforms, supports compress+buffer to disk. Cons: newer than Fluent Bit, fewer community plugins (but covers what we need).
- Fluent Bit: extremely lightweight, stable. Cons: less expressive transforms, trickier to maintain complex parsing rules.
- Filebeat: good for ELK heavy shops; heavier on resources.

Upgrade plan (OTEL, Prometheus operator, Grafana) — sequence and gating:
1) Pre-flight: run 'tf plan' in staging; validate Helm chart versions and CRDs. Back up PVCs (snapshot) for Prometheus TSDB and Grafana SQLite DB.
2) Rollout OTEL agent changes as config-only (no image bumps) to ensure config compiles.
3) Deploy relay as secondary with new version; bump agents to write to both old and new relays (dual-write) for 24-72 hours. Monitor errors/latency.
4) Promote new relay to be primary in LB, decommission old relay after traffic drains.
5) For Prometheus/Thanos: upgrade sidecars one by one, then upgrade Thanos store/compactor with canary. Ensure compactor retention and downsampling settings are preserved.
6) Grafana: import dashboards to staging Grafana first; then apply to prod via provisioning + swap LB target for blue/green if available.

Rollback strategy:
- Keep previous Helm chart manifests and image tags pinned. Use dual-write and feature flags to revert without losing data. For Prometheus TSDB corruption, restore from last snapshot and bring up a fresh Prometheus pointing at restored PVC.

Smoke tests and KPIs after rollout:
- Agent->relay latency (<200ms p95), relay error rate <0.1%.
- Prometheus scrape success rate >99% over 5m window.
- Thanos compactor backlog length < X segments (TBD).
- Grafana provisioning applied successfully and dashboards render in <2s.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default retention for on-prem customers (14d vs 30d).
- Confirm whether to include Cortex as alternate path in tf modules (cost model needed).
- Finalize auth model: mTLS + Vault-issued certs vs JWT short-lived tokens.
- Test Vector log buffering behavior under network partitions (simulate).

Runbook snippets / commands:
- Prometheus snapshot: kubectl exec -n monitoring prometheus-0 -- promtool tsdb create-blocks-from --dir=/prometheus "--from=..." (placeholder, verify exact command per chart).
- Force scrape config reload: curl -s -XPOST http://<prometheus>/-/reload
- OTEL relay health: kubectl get deploy otel-relay -n telemetry -o wide; kubectl logs deploy/otel-relay -c relay | tail -n 200

Notes from discussions: 
- Slack thread (2025-11-02): Ethan: prefer Vector for binary simplicity; Ravi: worried about Vector's operator maturity; Sofia: we should prioritize a 2-node HA relay in bare-metal installs.
- GH PR #834 contains initial tf-module scaffolding for otel-collector and relay. Good reference for variable names and outputs.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above.

If you are reviewing: focus feedback on the Terraform module boundaries and the upgrade sequence (are steps granular enough? what safety gates missing?).
